root_cause: Not a bug: a maintainer (willmcgugan) restyled Markdown rendering for rich 14.3.0 by taste. The statement (title 'Update to markdown styles', body 'Updates to Markdown styling') carries no spec; the only record of the intended look is the hidden ANSI snapshot tests.
best_solution: Merged fix: (1) default_styles.py: markdown.h1 bold+underline, h2 magenta underline, h3 magenta bold, h4 magenta italic, h5 italic, h6 dim; item.bullet bold only, item.number cyan, hr dim; new markdown.table.border (cyan) and markdown.table.header (cyan, bold=False). (2) markdown.py: Heading no longer wraps h1 in a HEAVY Panel and no longer adds a blank line before h2; it copies the text and justifies it from a LEVEL_ALIGN map (h1 center, others left). The rule renders as Rule(characters='-') followed by a blank Text(). The table uses box.SIMPLE, pad_edge=False, show_edge=True, collapse_padding=True, style='markdown.table.border', and each header cell is stylized with markdown.table.header. None of these values can be derived from the statement. The only way to reproduce them is the CHANGELOG wording in the PR ('changed style of headers/tables/rules, added markdown.table.header and markdown.table.border') plus the snapshot strings.
acceptable_alternatives: None in practice. The tests compare full rendered ANSI strings byte for byte, so any other color, box, justify or padding choice fails.
hidden_test_demands: Exact ANSI snapshot equality in tests/test_markdown.py::test_markdown_render, test_markdown_table, test_inline_styles_in_table, test_inline_styles_with_justification, test_partial_table, and tests/test_markdown_no_hyperlinks.py::test_markdown_render, plus an updated tests/_card_render.py expected string. Examples: h1 = centered '\x1b[1;4mHeading' with no panel border; h2 = left-aligned '\x1b[4;35m'; h3 '\x1b[1;35m'; h4 '\x1b[3;35m'; table borders '\x1b[36m' with SIMPLE box (thin rule), header cells cyan non-bold, collapsed padding; hr drawn with '-' then a blank line.
locating_signals: Only the word 'Markdown styles' points to rich/markdown.py and the markdown.* entries in rich/default_styles.py. No function, style name or value is named. The CHANGELOG in the upstream PR (not shown to the agent) names headers, tables, rules and the two new style keys.
our_outcome_summary: Failed under all four configs (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass false). v4, v6 and v7 produced empty patches (30/32/15 calls, 37-71 s). v8 (41 calls, 304 s, 1022 chars) guessed a different restyle: it changed markdown.code, code_block, block_quote and link/link_url colors and left headings, hr and tables untouched. All 6 snapshot tests failed (h1 still drawn in a HEAVY panel, tables still SIMPLE_HEAVY with bold headers).
generalizable_lesson: When a statement is a bare title like 'update X styles' with no values, the hidden tests are almost always golden snapshots of the maintainer's taste, so the target cannot be derived. Triage it early and cap the effort. If anything is attempted, read the existing snapshot tests to find which renderables they cover (here headings, tables, rules) and change those rather than unrelated styles. Do not burn the step budget exploring. A cheap, low-odds guess is fine, but an empty patch and a wrong guess score the same.
